│ ## MARKET VALUE                                                                                                                                                                   │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ This definition is in compliance with the OCC (Office of the Comptroller of the Currency), FDIC (Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation), 12 CFR part 34.42 FIRREA (Federal        │
│ Institutions Reforms, Recovery, and Enforcement Act), and USPAP (Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice) as adopted by the Appraisal Foundation and the Appraisal   │
│ Institute. This definition complies with the USPAP Regulations.¹                                                                                                                  │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ Market value is the major focus of most real property appraisal assignments. Both economic and legal definitions of market value have been developed and refined. A current       │
│ economic definition agreed upon by federal financial institutions of the United States of America is:                                                                             │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ The most probable price which a property should bring in a competitive and open market under all conditions requisite to a fair sale, the buyer and seller each acting prudently  │
│ and knowledgeably, and assuming the price is not affected by undue stimulus. Implicit in this definition is the consummation of a Sale as of a specified date and the passing of  │
│ title from seller to buyer under conditions whereby:                                                                                                                              │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ 1) Buyer and seller are typically motivated;                                                                                                                                      │
│ 2) Both parties are well informed or well advised, and acting in what they consider their best interests;                                                                         │
│ 3) A reasonable time is allowed for exposure in the open market;                                                                                                                  │
│ 4) Payment is made in terms of cash in United States dollars or in terms of financial arrangements comparable thereto; and                                                        │
│ 5) The price represents the normal consideration for the property sold unaffected by special or creative financing or Sale concessions granted by anyone associated with the      │
│ sale.                                                                                                                                                                             │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ Substitution of another currency for United States dollars in the fourth condition is appropriate in countries or in reports addressed to clients from other countries.²          │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ 126JG-111                                                                                                                                                                         │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │

│ ## DEFINITIONS³                                                                                                                                                                   │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ ### As Is Value                                                                                                                                                                   │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ The value of specific ownership rights to an identified parcel of real estate as of the effective date of the appraisal; relates to what physically exists and is legally         │
│ permissible and excludes all assumptions concerning hypothetical market conditions or possible rezoning.                                                                          │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ ### Hypothetical Condition                                                                                                                                                        │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ That which is contrary to what exists but is supposed for the purpose of analysis. Hypothetical conditions assume conditions contrary to known facts about physical, legal, or    │
│ economic characteristics of the subject property, or about conditions external to the property such as market conditions or trends, or about the integrity of data used in an     │
│ analysis. A hypothetical condition may be used in an assignment only if:                                                                                                          │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ - Use of the hypothetical condition is clearly required for legal purposes, for purposes of reasonable analysis, or for purposes of comparison;                                   │
│ - Use of the hypothetical condition results in a credible analysis; and                                                                                                           │
│ - The appraiser complies with the disclosure requirements set forth in USPAP for hypothetical conditions.                                                                         │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ ### Prospective Value                                                                                                                                                             │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ A forecast of the value expected at a specified future date. A prospective value estimate is most frequently sought in connection with real estate projects that are proposed,    │
│ under construction, or under conversion to a new use, or those that have not achieved sellout or a stabilized level of long-term occupancy at the time the appraisal report is    │
│ written.                                                                                                                                                                          │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ ### Stabilized Value                                                                                                                                                              │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ A value estimate that excludes from consideration any transitory condition, e.g., a bonus or premium for material, the abnormal inefficiency of labor, the cost of delay, or      │
│ unfinished repairs.                                                                                                                                                               │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ ### Fee Simple Estate                                                                                                                                                             │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ Absolute ownership unencumbered by any other interest or estate, subject only to the limitations imposed by the governmental powers of taxation, eminent domain, police power,    │
│ and escheat.                                                                                                                                                                      │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ ### Leased Fee Estate                                                                                                                                                             │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ An ownership interest held by a landlord with the rights of use and occupancy conveyed by lease to others. The rights of lessor (leased fee owner) and the leased fee are         │
│ specified by contract terms contained within the lease.                                                                                                                           │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ ### Leasehold Estate                                                                                                                                                              │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ An ownership interest held by the lessee (tenant or renter) through a lease conveying the rights of use and occupancy for a stated term under certain conditions.                 │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │

│ |  April 19, 2005 | Cambridge-Trinity, LLC | JB Equities, LLC & SJ Investments, LLC | $4,700,000  |                                                                               │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ Subject Listing History: The overall portfolio, consisting of the subject property and the adjacent 30-unit Trinity Plaza, is currently listed for $6,450,000, reflecting an      │
│ asking rate of $120.94 per square foot. According to Greg Frick of HFORE, the listing broker, the portfolio was initially brought to market several years ago at $8,900,000 and   │
│ received multiple offers ranging from $5,000,000 to $6,000,000. The price has been reduced several times, with the most recent adjustment to the current list price occurring     │
│ several months ago. No allocation was provided for the subject property alone; however, applying the asking rate of $120.94 per square foot to the subject's gross leasable area  │
│ results in an illustrative value indication of approximately $4,380,000, which is slightly below the original purchase price. This dip is reflective of the decline of retail     │
│ viability in the subject's micro market along W. Burnside Street.                                                                                                                 │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ The subject has remained on the market for an extended period, influenced by broader challenges in the downtown market, including civil unrest and an increasing homeless         │
│ population. These conditions have negatively affected investor sentiment and tenant demand, particularly for retail space, though gradual improvement has been reported. The      │
│ apartment component is comparatively better positioned, with ongoing unit updates and market-level rents, though it reflects an 8.16% vacancy rate (two rent-ready units and two  │
│ down units). The retail portion contains two long-term vacancies totaling 4,082 square feet, representing 62.35% of the retail area.                                              │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ Given the prolonged marketing exposure exceeding two years and the absence of a pending or closed transaction, the current list price appears above market expectations. The      │
│ significant retail vacancy and the lower achievable lease rates for the vacant suites further suggest that additional price reductions may be necessary to attract investors. As  │
│ such, this listing provides a limited and less reliable value indicator for the subject property, and the allocation derived from the asking price should be considered           │
│ illustrative only.                                                                                                                                                                │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │

│ # VALUATION METHODOLOGY                                                                                                                                                           │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ The Income and Sales Comparison Approaches are performed and reconciled to develop our opinion of the Prospective Leased Fee Value at Stabilized Occupancy. Deductions for        │
│ absorption (includes income loss from rent increases and deferred maintenance) are made to reconcile the As Is Leased Fee Value of the subject property. The Cost Approach was    │
│ not presented in this appraisal due to the subjectivity and difficulty in determining accrued depreciation for older buildings. A typical purchaser of the subject property would │
│ not consider this approach as a reliable indicator. Therefore, the exclusion of this valuation approach is reasonable and does not reduce the credibility of this appraisal.      │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │

│ ## MARKETING AND EXPOSURE TIME                                                                                                                                                    │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ Marketing time is the period of time it takes an interest in real property to sell on the market subsequent to the date of an appraisal. Exposure time is the estimated length of │
│ time the property interest being appraised would have been on the market prior to the hypothetical consummation of a sale at market value on the effective date of appraisal. The │
│ market and exposure periods are deemed to be equivalent. Discussions with brokers active in the market indicate that there is stable demand for well-located, functional          │
│ properties in the immediate subject area. The sale comparables presented below are noted along with the anticipated marketing and exposure period.                                │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ |  Property Type | Comparables- Marketing and Exposure | Forecast- Market and Exposure  |                                                                                         │
│ | --- | --- | --- |                                                                                                                                                               │
│ |  Mixed-Use Developments | Unknown/137 Days to 2 Years | 365 Days or Less  |                                                                                                     │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ The subject (plus Trinity Plaza) has been on the market for over 2 years, initially priced at $8,900,000. Offers ranged between $5,000,000 and $6,000,000 at the time. The price  │
│ has dropped consistently to a current list price of $6,450,000. If the price isn't dropped, the extended marketing period will increase. Overall, this is not a good indicator    │
│ for the subject, with the current allocated list price ($4,380,000) being 11.73% higher than the concluded As-Is Leased Fee Value. Based on the subject's physical and location   │
│ characteristics, the subject's marketing time and the comparables, marketing and exposure periods are noted above. This assumes that the subject property was competently         │
│ promoted and appropriately priced.                                                                                                                                                │

│ The subject property is located in the city of Portland. The Portland area is bounded by the Columbia River/Vancouver Washington to the north, Gresham to the east, West Linn /   │
│ Lake Oswego / Milwaukee to the south, Beaverton / Tigard to the west.                                                                                                             │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │

│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ ## General Neighborhood                                                                                                                                                           │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ The Greater Portland Oregon Central Business District (CBD), often referred to as Downtown Portland, serves as the city's primary commercial core and economic hub. It is         │
│ characterized by a mix of high-rise office towers, government buildings, financial institutions, retail corridors, hotels, cultural venues, and transit-oriented development. The │
│ area features excellent multimodal access, including MAX light rail, streetcar lines, buses, and bike infrastructure, supporting high walkability scores and strong commuter      │
│ flows. Real estate in the CBD includes a predominance of Class A and B office space, mixed-use buildings with ground-floor retail, and residential high-rises or condos in        │
│ adaptive reuse projects. The market appeals to professionals seeking urban convenience, with proximity to landmarks such as Pioneer Courthouse Square, the Portland Art Museum,   │
│ theaters, and the Willamette River waterfront. Property values benefit from institutional demand, though influenced by broader urban trends including office vacancy dynamics and │
│ residential densification.                                                                                                                                                        │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ ## Immediate Area Overview                                                                                                                                                        │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ The subject property is located in Uptown Portland within the broader Northwest District (commonly referred to as Nob Hill or the Alphabet District). This area lies just         │
│ northwest of the CBD and adjacent to the Pearl District, placing it within a desirable transition zone between the intensity of downtown and established residential              │
│ neighborhoods. The district's commercial core, centered on NW 21st and NW 23rd Avenues, are characterized by pedestrian-oriented retail, restaurants, and services, supported by  │
│ a mix of historic homes and early- to mid-century multifamily buildings. The nearby Pearl District contributes additional appeal through modern residential development, office   │
│ uses, cultural amenities, and green spaces. The location offers convenient access to the CBD, employment centers, and transit.                                                    │

│ These factors have influenced real estate performance. Office uses have been most affected, with retail also impacted by reduced daytime workforce activity. Apartment properties │
│ have generally re-stabilized, though with slower rent growth and modestly higher turnover. Retail vacancy remains evident along West Burnside, including several long-term        │

│ ## OUTLOOK AND CONCLUSION                                                                                                                                                         │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ Neighborhoods are constantly changing and continually cycle through four phases. The four phases include growth, stability, decline, and renewal. These phases are used to        │
│ evaluate the changes that occur within a neighborhood over time. During the growth phase, the neighborhood is in the beginning of development and expansion. Following the growth │
│ phase is stability. The neighborhood may still grow, but at a much slower pace. A neighborhood enters a state of decline when it can no longer compete with adjacent              │
│ neighborhoods. Lastly, renewal is the period during which a neighborhood is "rediscovered" because of affordability and convenience. The subject area has been in the             │
│ growth/renewal phase as a long standing commercial and residential area locally, but showing signs of decline as businesses leaving the downtown core is still ongoing.           │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ As the population and employment rates keep trending slowly upward, the subject market area is anticipated to continue improving, with appreciating property values in the long   │
│ term. The adjacent table outlines some of the crucial neighborhood components that both institutional and private investors consider.                                             │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │

│ HIGHEST AND BEST USE ANALYSIS                                                                                                                                                     │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ The Appraisal Institute defines the concept of highest and best use as follows:                                                                                                   │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ "The reasonably probable and legal use of vacant land or an improved property, which is physically possible, appropriately supported, financially feasible, and results in the    │
│ highest value. The four criteria the highest and best use must meet are legal permissibility, physical possibility, financial feasibility, and maximum profitability." 4          │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ The highest and best use concept is based on traditional appraisal theory and reflects the attitudes of typical buyers and sellers who recognize that value is predicated on      │
│ anticipation of future benefits. This theory is based on the wealth maximization of the owner. In the appraisal process, highest and best use concept typically reflects most     │
│ probable use, and often relates to the most probable value of the property.                                                                                                       │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ # AS VACANT                                                                                                                                                                       │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ The subject is zoned CXd (Central Commercial w/ design overlay), city of Portland Planning Department. The Central Commercial (CXd) zone is intended to provide for commercial    │
│ and mixed use development within Portland's most urban and intense areas, specifically the Central City and the Gateway Regional Center. A broad range of uses are allowed to     │
│ reflect Portland's role as a commercial, cultural, residential, and governmental center. Development is intended to be very intense with high building coverage, large buildings, │
│ and buildings placed close together. Development is intended to be pedestrian-oriented with a strong emphasis on a safe and attractive streetscape. The Design overlay zone is    │
│ applied to this zone. This zone allows a mix of commercial and residential uses (limitations set at 15,000 SF for industrial warehouse uses.                                      │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ ![img-38.jpeg](img-38.jpeg)                                                                                                                                                       │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ Legal / Physical: Basic Zoning Requirements; Minimum Density – None. Maximum Density – 4 to 1 FAR. Building Height – 75'. Site Coverage – 100% maximum, with none for             │
│ landscaping. Overall, there is the potential for additional size/height with bonus provisions. Considering it location along a major arterial, a retail component would most      │
│ likely, however, based on the current market, despite the temporarily high apartment vacancy, apartments are more likely. The subject is physically suitable for development,     │
│ with functional / marketable land area and topography. In addition, the subject parcel is physically functional, with good exposure and linkages, and would have average appeal   │
│ for development. With a site size of 0.23 acres (10,000 SF) a maximum development up to a total size of 40,000 SF (without bonus provisions) would be allowed.                    │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ Feasibility: Apartment uses in the subject's market area consist of older and newer (New to 100+ years) commercial buildings in this historic area, with average finishes and     │
│ amenities. The rent levels are stable with vacancy rate used by brokers and owners at 5%, which includes credit loss.                                                             │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ 126JG-111                                                                                                                                                                         │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │

│ Commercial uses in the subject's market area consist of older and newer (New to 100+ years) commercial buildings in this historic area, with average finishes and amenities. The  │

│ ## As-Vacant Conclusion                                                                                                                                                           │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ Based on the surrounding developments, current rental market trends noting some positive traits despite the continued civil unrest in portions of the downtown core, the highest  │
│ and best use for the subject as vacant would be for apartment uses (based on slower demand for commercial uses).                                                                  │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ ## AS IMPROVED                                                                                                                                                                    │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ The subject as a combined mixed-use development (49 apartment units and 4 retail suites totaling 45,704 SF GBA), the subject is a legal, but non-conforming use (above the        │
│ maximum FAR). Considering the subject's age and location, this is not atypical. If a nonconforming use is discontinued for 3 continuous years, the nonconforming use rights are   │
│ lost. When a structure containing a nonconforming use is damaged by fire or other causes beyond the control of the owner, the re-establishment of the nonconforming use is        │
│ prohibited if the repair cost of the structure is more than 75 percent of its assessed value. The marketing activity experienced by developments in the subject's general market  │
│ area demonstrates market acceptance of properties with features and physical characteristics similar to the subject. The subject is an average quality mixed-use project with     │
│ average utility and local significance. It offers typical unit amenities with a functional and efficient design. The neighborhood characteristics have been previously described, │
│ and are also supportive of the current use.                                                                                                                                       │

│ # VALUATION APPROACHES                                                                                                                                                            │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ The Cost Approach was not presented in this appraisal due to the subjectivity and difficulty in determining accrued depreciation for older buildings. A typical purchaser of the  │
│ subject property would not consider this approach as a reliable indicator. Therefore, the exclusion of this valuation approach is reasonable and does not reduce the credibility  │
│ of this appraisal.                                                                                                                                                                │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ The Income Capitalization Approach is the process of converting the anticipated income of a property to value by a process known as capitalization. This method converts a        │
│ periodic series of future benefits (net income) into a present value by use of an appropriate, market derived, rate of return. The market capitalization rate reflects the        │
│ specific income pattern, return on investment, and change in the value of the investment. The Income Capitalization Approach is considered to reflect common investor behavior,   │
│ and is typically an accurate measure of the value of income-producing properties.                                                                                                 │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ The Sales Comparison Approach is the value derived by comparing the subject property to similar properties that have sold recently, applying appropriate units of comparison, and │
│ making necessary adjustments to the sales prices. This approach may be used to value vacant land or improved properties. It is most reliable for special use and owner occupied   │
│ properties that are not typically purchased based on income producing ability. This approach is used for the valuation of the improvements.                                       │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ # VALUE CONCLUSION                                                                                                                                                                │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ The income and sales comparison approaches are performed and reconciled to develop our opinion of the Prospective Leased Fee Value at Stabilized Occupancy, with adjustments made │
│ to reconcile the As-Is Leased Fee Value.                                                                                                                                          │

│ ## COMPARABLE RENT ANALYSIS: APARTMENTS                                                                                                                                           │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ The following analysis generally ranks the subject among the comparables using tangible dollar/percentage adjustments to illustrate the relative comparability to the subject.    │
│ The comparables are adjusted to the subject property consistent with standard valuation (appraisal) methodology. A positive percentage adjustment indicates that a comparable is  │
│ inferior to the subject regarding a specific (or set of related) characteristics) and is therefore adjusted upward to simulate rough parity with the subject property.            │
│ Conversely, negative dollar/percentage adjustment-indicates-that a comparable is superior to the subject in some regard and so is adjusted downward. The resulting range of       │
│ adjusted indicators provides a quantifiable illustration of the subjective-logic-upon-which the comparable analysis is based. The conclusion-is further refined in the narrative  │
│ analysis that follows.                                                                                                                                                            │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │

│ ## OVERALL CAPITALIZATION RATE ANALYSIS                                                                                                                                           │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ The following analysis generally ranks the subject among the comparables using tangible percentage adjustments to illustrate the relative comparability to the subject. The       │
│ comparables are adjusted to the subject property consistent with standard valuation (appraisal) methodology. A positive percentage adjustment indicates that a comparable is      │
│ inferior to the subject regarding a specific (or set of related) characteristics) and is therefore adjusted upward to simulate rough parity with the subject property.            │
│ Conversely, negative percentage adjustment-indicates-that a comparable is superior to the subject in some regard and so is adjusted downward. The resulting range of adjusted     │
│ indicators provides a quantifiable illustration of the subjective logic upon which the comparable analysis is based. The conclusion-is further refined in the narrative analysis  │
│ that follows.                                                                                                                                                                     │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ Market Extraction Analysis: Overall capitalization rates are market-extracted by dividing the net operating income of a sold property by its cash-equivalent sale price. The      │
│ primary factors influencing capitalization rates are: 1) The quality and certainty ('durability') of the net operating income stream; 2) risk factors; 3) physical and location   │
│ characteristics of the property; 4) the competitive market position of the property; and 5) the potential for future appreciation. Capitalization rate comparables are summarized │
│ on the following table (next page). The unadjusted comparable sales used in this analysis have a moderate range between 5.19% and 7.60%. The following presents the analysis      │
│ outlining the individual adjustments made to arrive at an adjusted rate range for the subject and a concluded capitalization rate.                                                │

│ INCOME CAPITALIZATION APPROACH (continued)                                                                                                                                        │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ Income Stability: (Location/Rent Levels) – This adjustment is intended to account for differences in the types and/or quality of income streams based on locational attributes    │
│ and rent levels. For instance, a comparable located in an area of higher demand/superior income levels, poses lower risk for turnover and rent drops in a recessionary market.    │
│ Adjustments between -7.5% and 10.0% were made.                                                                                                                                    │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ Building Class: (Effects on Investor Expectations) – This adjustment is intended to account for differences in income potential as it pertains to its quality and/or condition.   │
│ For instance, high quality and well maintained properties tend to maintain market rents as opposed to lower quality developments (including the potential for higher maintenance, │
│ effecting the net operating income). Adjustments between -7.5% and 15.0% were made.                                                                                               │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ Development Size: (Liquidity/Economies of Scale) – This adjustment is intended to account for differences in development sizes and their liquidity potential. For instance, all   │
│ else being equal, a smaller development typically has higher demand (financing options/larger investor pool). Therefore, adjustments between 30.0% and -10.0% were made.          │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ Market Condition (Financing / Market Events/Demand) – This adjustment is intended to reflect intangible factors that affect marketability such as the availability of financing,  │
│ atypical market events, and the demand for the property type. So far, according to several brokers interviewed, prices haven't significantly dropped because of those factors,    │
│ but time will tell how long the market will shrug off these conditions. Overall, no adjustments were made.                                                                        │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ Summary: The adjusted comparables range between 7.27% and 7.81%. The lower portion of the range is not typical and generally reflective of all cash buyers, which are able to     │
│ purchase the investments at a lower capitalization rate (no lending restraints). This is a good indicator of investor anticipations of the market, but not reflective of a        │
│ typical buyer needing loans considering the price points of mixed-use (apartments over commercial) in the market area. Although capitalizations rates have been ticking upwards   │
│ (even for cash buyers to some extent) as a reflection of the current market, this is anticipated to stabilize over the next 12 months.                                            │

│ v. Nondiscrimination                                                                                                                                                              │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ The Fair Housing Act, Equal Credit Opportunity Act, and other federal, state, and local laws and regulations broadly prohibit discrimination in real estate appraisal and lending │
│ services based on legally protected characteristics. These protected characteristics, depending on the applicable law or regulation, may include race, color, religion, sex,      │
│ sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital status, disability, familial status, exercise of any federally protected civil right, receipt of income derived from any public │
│ assistance program, birthplaces of residents of the property or in the neighborhood, national origin of the prospective owners or occupants of the subject property or of the     │
│ present owners or occupants of the properties in the vicinity of the subject property.                                                                                            │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ In accepting this assignment, you acknowledge the importance of these protections against discrimination and agree that your performance of the assignment, including without     │
│ limitation your development and reporting of the appraisal and your interactions with all persons, will not be based in part or in whole on information involving any legally     │
│ protected characteristics, regardless of your intention, unless expressly permitted by law. You agree that you and persons acting under your direction or control are             │
│ knowledgeable of and will abide by all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations governing nondiscrimination.                                                     │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ Furthermore, in conformity with USPAP, if no law or regulation prohibits the use of or reliance upon a protected characteristic, then the use of or reliance upon that            │
│ characteristic is permitted only to the extent that it is both essential to the assignment and necessary for credible assignment results. See Exceptions.                         │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ 1. Specifically Prohibited/Unacceptable Practices                                                                                                                                 │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ To avoid discrimination, or a suggestion of discrimination, by you or by other parties who may utilize or rely on your appraisal, you agree that you will not:                    │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ a) Act with bias or otherwise discriminate against or treat differently any individual or group                                                                                   │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ ---                                                                                                                                                                               │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ ## Page 102                                                                                                                                                                       │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ based on a protected characteristic.                                                                                                                                              │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ b) Consider, discuss, or refer to any protected characteristic of any party or with regard to the neighborhood or community within which the subject property is located in your  │
│ appraisal development and/or report or in communications with other parties, including MountainSeed, unless expressly permitted by law or regulation.                             │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ c) Use, rely on, consider, or discuss in any analysis, opinion or conclusion, any assumptions, stereotypes, or generalizations related to protected characteristics (or           │
│ nonprotected characteristics intentionally used as a substitute for a protected characteristic).                                                                                  │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ d) Employ terminology or veiled language as code words that may signal underlying bias, including but not limited to desirable location/neighborhood, diverse, gentrified, pride  │
│ of ownership, predominantly White or Black or Hispanic neighborhood, services or amenities geared toward a protected class or using generational descriptors such as Gen X,       │
│ Millennial, or Boomer.                                                                                                                                                            │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ These specific unacceptable practices do not limit your responsibility to comply with all other discrimination prohibitions in the applicable laws and regulations.               │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ ## 2. Exceptions                                                                                                                                                                  │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ a) In limited circumstances, applicable nondiscrimination laws and regulations may permit the consideration of protected characteristics in the performance of an appraisal       │
│ (e.g., the prohibition against discrimination based on family may not be applicable to an appraisal of housing legally designated for older persons). If a protected              │
│ characteristic is considered under such a limited exception, that such consideration is required or expressly permitted by law or regulation, one must conspicuously state in any │
│ communication, report, or analysis (1) the protected characteristic(s) considered, (2) the law or regulation that requires or expressly permits consideration/discussion, and (3) │
│ demonstrate that this use is essential to the assignment and necessary for credible assignment results.                                                                           │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ b) If no law or regulation prohibits the use of or reliance upon a protected characteristic, then one must demonstrate that the use of or reliance upon that characteristic is    │
│ both essential to the assignment and necessary for credible assignment results.                                                                                                   │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │

│ MountainSeed in its investigation and resolution of the matter.                                                                                                                   │

│ ## MARKET VALUE                                                                                                                                                                   │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ This definition is in compliance with the OCC (Office of the Comptroller of the Currency), FDIC (Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation), 12 CFR part 34.42 FIRREA (Federal        │
│ Institutions Reforms, Recovery, and Enforcement Act), and USPAP (Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice) as adopted by the Appraisal Foundation and the Appraisal   │
│ Institute. This definition complies with the USPAP Regulations.¹                                                                                                                  │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ Market value is the major focus of most real property appraisal assignments. Both economic and legal definitions of market value have been developed and refined. A current       │
│ economic definition agreed upon by federal financial institutions of the United States of America is:                                                                             │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ The most probable price which a property should bring in a competitive and open market under all conditions requisite to a fair sale, the buyer and seller each acting prudently  │
│ and knowledgeably, and assuming the price is not affected by undue stimulus. Implicit in this definition is the consummation of a Sale as of a specified date and the passing of  │
│ title from seller to buyer under conditions whereby:                                                                                                                              │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ 1) Buyer and seller are typically motivated;                                                                                                                                      │
│ 2) Both parties are well informed or well advised, and acting in what they consider their best interests;                                                                         │
│ 3) A reasonable time is allowed for exposure in the open market;                                                                                                                  │
│ 4) Payment is made in terms of cash in United States dollars or in terms of financial arrangements comparable thereto; and                                                        │
│ 5) The price represents the normal consideration for the property sold unaffected by special or creative financing or Sale concessions granted by anyone associated with the      │
│ sale.                                                                                                                                                                             │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ Substitution of another currency for United States dollars in the fourth condition is appropriate in countries or in reports addressed to clients from other countries.²          │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ 126JG-111                                                                                                                                                                         │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ 16                                                                                                                                                                                │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │

│ ## DEFINITIONS³                                                                                                                                                                   │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ ### As Is Value                                                                                                                                                                   │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ The value of specific ownership rights to an identified parcel of real estate as of the effective date of the appraisal; relates to what physically exists and is legally         │
│ permissible and excludes all assumptions concerning hypothetical market conditions or possible rezoning.                                                                          │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ ### Hypothetical Condition                                                                                                                                                        │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ That which is contrary to what exists but is supposed for the purpose of analysis. Hypothetical conditions assume conditions contrary to known facts about physical, legal, or    │
│ economic characteristics of the subject property, or about conditions external to the property such as market conditions or trends, or about the integrity of data used in an     │
│ analysis. A hypothetical condition may be used in an assignment only if:                                                                                                          │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ - Use of the hypothetical condition is clearly required for legal purposes, for purposes of reasonable analysis, or for purposes of comparison;                                   │
│ - Use of the hypothetical condition results in a credible analysis; and                                                                                                           │
│ - The appraiser complies with the disclosure requirements set forth in USPAP for hypothetical conditions.                                                                         │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ ### Prospective Value                                                                                                                                                             │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ A forecast of the value expected at a specified future date. A prospective value estimate is most frequently sought in connection with real estate projects that are proposed,    │
│ under construction, or under conversion to a new use, or those that have not achieved sellout or a stabilized level of long-term occupancy at the time the appraisal report is    │
│ written.                                                                                                                                                                          │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ ### Stabilized Value                                                                                                                                                              │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ A value estimate that excludes from consideration any transitory condition, e.g., a bonus or premium for material, the abnormal inefficiency of labor, the cost of delay, or      │
│ unfinished repairs.                                                                                                                                                               │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ ### Fee Simple Estate                                                                                                                                                             │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ Absolute ownership unencumbered by any other interest or estate, subject only to the limitations imposed by the governmental powers of taxation, eminent domain, police power,    │
│ and escheat.                                                                                                                                                                      │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ ### Leased Fee Estate                                                                                                                                                             │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ An ownership interest held by a landlord with the rights of use and occupancy conveyed by lease to others. The rights of lessor (leased fee owner) and the leased fee are         │
│ specified by contract terms contained within the lease.                                                                                                                           │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ ### Leasehold Estate                                                                                                                                                              │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ An ownership interest held by the lessee (tenant or renter) through a lease conveying the rights of use and occupancy for a stated term under certain conditions.                 │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │

│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ A preliminary title report was not provided. Based on county records, title to the property is vested in Cambridge-Trinity, LLC, which has owned and operated the subject since   │
│ 2005. There are no other known transfers for the past 3 years.                                                                                                                    │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ |  Ownership (Past 3+ Years)  |   |   |   |                                                                                                                                       │

│ |  April 19, 2005 | Cambridge-Trinity, LLC | JB Equities, LLC & SJ Investments, LLC | $4,700,000  |                                                                               │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ Subject Listing History: The overall portfolio, consisting of the subject property and the adjacent 30-unit Trinity Plaza, is currently listed for $6,450,000, reflecting an      │
│ asking rate of $120.94 per square foot. According to Greg Frick of HFORE, the listing broker, the portfolio was initially brought to market several years ago at $8,900,000 and   │
│ received multiple offers ranging from $5,000,000 to $6,000,000. The price has been reduced several times, with the most recent adjustment to the current list price occurring     │
│ several months ago. No allocation was provided for the subject property alone; however, applying the asking rate of $120.94 per square foot to the subject's gross leasable area  │
│ results in an illustrative value indication of approximately $4,380,000, which is slightly below the original purchase price. This dip is reflective of the decline of retail     │
│ viability in the subject's micro market along W. Burnside Street.                                                                                                                 │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ The subject has remained on the market for an extended period, influenced by broader challenges in the downtown market, including civil unrest and an increasing homeless         │
│ population. These conditions have negatively affected investor sentiment and tenant demand, particularly for retail space, though gradual improvement has been reported. The      │
│ apartment component is comparatively better positioned, with ongoing unit updates and market-level rents, though it reflects an 8.16% vacancy rate (two rent-ready units and two  │
│ down units). The retail portion contains two long-term vacancies totaling 4,082 square feet, representing 62.35% of the retail area.                                              │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ Given the prolonged marketing exposure exceeding two years and the absence of a pending or closed transaction, the current list price appears above market expectations. The      │
│ significant retail vacancy and the lower achievable lease rates for the vacant suites further suggest that additional price reductions may be necessary to attract investors. As  │
│ such, this listing provides a limited and less reliable value indicator for the subject property, and the allocation derived from the asking price should be considered           │
│ illustrative only.                                                                                                                                                                │

│ # VALUATION METHODOLOGY                                                                                                                                                           │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ The Income and Sales Comparison Approaches are performed and reconciled to develop our opinion of the Prospective Leased Fee Value at Stabilized Occupancy. Deductions for        │
│ absorption (includes income loss from rent increases and deferred maintenance) are made to reconcile the As Is Leased Fee Value of the subject property. The Cost Approach was    │
│ not presented in this appraisal due to the subjectivity and difficulty in determining accrued depreciation for older buildings. A typical purchaser of the subject property would │
│ not consider this approach as a reliable indicator. Therefore, the exclusion of this valuation approach is reasonable and does not reduce the credibility of this appraisal.      │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ 126JG-111                                                                                                                                                                         │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │

│ ## MARKETING AND EXPOSURE TIME                                                                                                                                                    │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ Marketing time is the period of time it takes an interest in real property to sell on the market subsequent to the date of an appraisal. Exposure time is the estimated length of │
│ time the property interest being appraised would have been on the market prior to the hypothetical consummation of a sale at market value on the effective date of appraisal. The │
│ market and exposure periods are deemed to be equivalent. Discussions with brokers active in the market indicate that there is stable demand for well-located, functional          │
│ properties in the immediate subject area. The sale comparables presented below are noted along with the anticipated marketing and exposure period.                                │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ |  Property Type | Comparables- Marketing and Exposure | Forecast- Market and Exposure  |                                                                                         │
│ | --- | --- | --- |                                                                                                                                                               │
│ |  Mixed-Use Developments | Unknown/137 Days to 2 Years | 365 Days or Less  |                                                                                                     │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ The subject (plus Trinity Plaza) has been on the market for over 2 years, initially priced at $8,900,000. Offers ranged between $5,000,000 and $6,000,000 at the time. The price  │
│ has dropped consistently to a current list price of $6,450,000. If the price isn't dropped, the extended marketing period will increase. Overall, this is not a good indicator    │
│ for the subject, with the current allocated list price ($4,380,000) being 11.73% higher than the concluded As-Is Leased Fee Value. Based on the subject's physical and location   │
│ characteristics, the subject's marketing time and the comparables, marketing and exposure periods are noted above. This assumes that the subject property was competently         │
│ promoted and appropriately priced.                                                                                                                                                │

│ negatively affect the value of the subject.                                                                                                                                       │

│ adverse conditions or defects that would adversely affect the value of the subject. Deferred maintenance conclusions are based on this premise and assumed to accurate.           │

│ The Appraisal Institute defines market area as following: "The geographic or locational delineation of the market for a specific category of real estate, i.e., the area in which │
│ alternative, similar properties effectively compete with the subject property in the minds of probable, potential purchasers and buyers".                                         │
│                                                                                                                                                                                   │
│ The market area analysis is presented in two sections, a regional analysis and general neighborhood analysis. The regional analysis will focus on a macro view of the subject     │
│ market area and generally highlight current conditions that shape the nature of the regional economy. A more specific analysis that focuses on the subject's neighborhood area    │
│ will follow.                                                                                                                                                                      │
